rule: GOAL: Match the target color sequence by filling empty slots in order. CONTROLS: Click a colored chip to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: Placing a chip swaps it with the gray dot in that slot. TRAP: Thinking you must click a confirm button; placement is instant upon clicking the slot.

GOAL: Align two crosses to cover specific dots by moving them into precise positions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected cross; spacebar switches between the two crosses. RULE: Both crosses must simultaneously cover all dots with their arms to clear the level. TRAP: Assuming arms shrink permanently when hitting the board edge; they only clip visually but restore length when moving away.

GOAL: Clear the level in two actions. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the paddle; space launched the ball. RULE: The ball’s speed doubled instantly after hitting the block. TRAP: Thinking the ball bounced normally; it actually accelerated straight down, skipping the return trip.

GOAL: Slide the plug along the wall to align with the hole. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons move the cursor horizontally along the boundary. RULE: The plug only fits when the cursor aligns perfectly with the gap. TRAP: Thinking the walls were independent obstacles instead of a single sliding track.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the target cell using exactly three moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the character one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Movement is blocked by solid walls and requires clear paths between adjacent tiles. TRAP: Assuming a direct route exists; verify connectivity first, as hidden walls can make the shortest visual path impossible.

GOAL: Guide three distinct shapes to collect every colored dot scattered across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently selected shape; the space bar cycles selection between shapes. RULE: A dot vanishes only when a shape’s arm passes directly over it during movement. TRAP: Assuming you must move all shapes to a central point wastes turns; each shape only needs to cover its specific color dots.

GOAL: Extend two colored bars to touch their respective cross targets simultaneously. CONTROLS: Click the arrow next to each bar to extend or retract its length. RULE: The level only completes when both dots land exactly on their crosses at the same time. TRAP: Assuming a single bar reaching its target triggers a win wastes actions, as the other bar must also be positioned correctly.

GOAL: Move the green plug horizontally to align perfectly with the target hole on the wall. CONTROLS: Left button shifts the plug left; right button shifts the plug right. RULE: Each click moves the plug by a fixed distance; only column alignment matters, not vertical position. TRAP: Believing vertical movement is needed or that the plug must be centered visually rather than aligned to the specific hole coordinates.

GOAL: Sort letters to match colored slots. CONTROLS: Click a slot to pick up its letter, click another to swap them. RULE: The displaced letter always lands in the slot you just left. TRAP: Thinking you must click the original slot again; the new carrier stays in the target, ready for the next move.

GOAL: Fill the red box slots with letters while routing through side boxes to match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Click letters from the bottom palette, then click empty gray slots inside the boxes to place them. RULE: Read the path sequentially: red slots before a ring, then the linked color box, then the next red slot. TRAP: Assuming rings are just decorations; they are actually ports that force you to visit the matching color box.

GOAL: Arrange chips to match a target color sequence across linked boxes. CONTROLS: Click chips to select, click slots to place, press Space to confirm. RULE: A ring in the outer box diverts the sequence into the inner box, preserving internal order. TRAP: Assuming the ring consumes a sequence position; it only blocks the slot and triggers the diversion.

GOAL: Slide the ink blob left into the print head to fill it. CONTROLS: Left arrow moves the blob two columns left; bar decreases per move. RULE: The blob must physically touch the head region to transfer color. TRAP: Do not click the panels directly; they are passive outputs, not interactive targets.

GOAL: Position three frames into the target slots to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player and carry the attached frame; Space attaches or releases the frame. RULE: Frames must be pushed into the designated blue zone to win. TRAP: Assuming you can place frames anywhere; they only stick to the specific target slots.

GOAL: Place chips and rings so the sequence of visited slots matches a hidden target pattern, with the blue ring visited twice. CONTROLS: Click a chip to pick it up, click a slot to place it, and press space to verify the solution. RULE: The two blue visits must produce identical three-chip sequences in the target pattern, forcing the rings into adjacent red slots. TRAP: Assuming the blue ring visits are independent; they are linked, requiring the same chip pattern before and after the middle red slots.

GOAL: Match the hidden pattern on the eight-by-eight grid by toggling the five keys. CONTROLS: Click each key to flip its color between black and white. RULE: The yellow brackets show the target shape, which aligns with the center column. TRAP: I wasted time searching for complex interactions between keys, but they are independent.

GOAL: Fill three sub-boxes by matching their pre-filled chips to specific target sequences. CONTROLS: Space confirms placement; drag rings to red slots to set visit order; drag chips to empty slots. RULE: The ring order dictates which sub-box receives which target sequence, linking first-slot colors to specific windows. TRAP: Assuming ring order is irrelevant; placing rings incorrectly assigns wrong sequences to sub-boxes, breaking the match.

GOAL: Shrink the four-by-four blob to pass the narrow valve and reach the head. CONTROLS: Click white panel cells to match the yellow pattern; use arrows to move the blob. RULE: Lighting the exact yellow pattern triggers a print event that halves the blob’s size. TRAP: Assuming rotation or splitting solves the width limit; only pattern completion shrinks the shape.

GOAL: Rotate a bracket to the correct angle by moving between columns and pressing UP to cycle through positions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor between columns; UP rotates the bracket clockwise. RULE: Each column requires a specific number of UP presses to reach the target shape; the total actions equal the sum of these presses plus cursor moves. TRAP: Assuming all columns need the same number of presses wastes time; some columns require zero or minimal adjustments.

GOAL: Move shapes to cover all red dots simultaneously to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space toggles the active shape. RULE: Victory only triggers when every dot is hidden at the exact same moment. TRAP: Assuming dots vanish individually upon contact; partial coverage yields no progress.

GOAL: Align three plugs by shifting fluid between five columns. CONTROLS: Click channels to move two units between adjacent columns. RULE: Fluid stops rising if it hits the lower wall height of its column. TRAP: Ignoring wall heights causes overflow, forcing you to waste moves draining excess fluid.

GOAL: Place chips to match target sequences across three colored boxes. CONTROLS: Space to select and place items; click to move cursor. RULE: Rings placed in a box divert their contents to the box matching the ring's color. TRAP: Assuming rings stay in their placed box; they actually redirect chips to the matching color box.

GOAL: Rotate seven distinct shapes to match hidden targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor and spin the active shape. RULE: Each slot holds a different symbol; only exact matches count. TRAP: Assuming any rotation of a shape works will fail the puzzle.

GOAL: Match eight yellow symbols to seven blue slots using legend groups. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cursor to select and swap symbol positions. RULE: Each yellow group maps to a specific blue group size from the key. TRAP: Assuming one-to-one pairing caused errors; some yellow groups map to multiple blue slots or vice versa.

GOAL: Guide the token along the path to the target blob. CONTROLS: Click a path dot to move the token toward it. RULE: The token only moves if the click is within three dots. TRAP: Clicking distant dots fails; assume the pulse shows range, not just feedback.

GOAL: Fill the blue strip with correct glyph rotations to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys cycle through shapes; UP finalizes the selection. RULE: Any valid rotation of the target shape is accepted as correct. TRAP: Believing you must find the exact original orientation, wasting time on unnecessary cycles.

GOAL: Position the orange dot exactly onto the green cross target. CONTROLS: Click side buttons to extend or retract colored bars in cardinal directions. RULE: Bars push adjacent bars, but stop immediately if they hit a wall or another bar. TRAP: Assuming bars can slide through corners or pass through each other; they cannot.

GOAL: Push the red block right to clear the corridor and reach the green exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; moving into the block pushes it one space if open. RULE: The block is solid but movable; it does not instantly kill on contact. TRAP: Believing the block was a lethal wall forced a search for impossible paths.

GOAL: Extend the arm to hit the remaining target. CONTROLS: Arrows extend or retract the arm; blocks stick to the tip when retracting but stay behind when extending. RULE: A hit registers only when the arm pierces a target during extension. TRAP: Thinking a block moves with the arm when extending; it actually stays put, leaving the tip to pass through empty space.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to the highlighted corner. CONTROLS: Red arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; green rotates it clockwise. RULE: Each click moves every block one slot along the perimeter. TRAP: Assuming you could move blocks individually or change their order; you can only shift the entire ring.

GOAL: Match the active grid’s outer colors to its center mini-pattern, turning specific cells red to mirror the white spots. CONTROLS: Click outer cells to toggle them between blue and red until the pattern aligns perfectly with the center guide. RULE: The center mini-pattern acts as a stencil: white marks mean red, gray marks mean blue for the surrounding eight cells. TRAP: Assuming the center cell itself needs changing or that the pattern rotates, rather than treating it as a static template.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single peg. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click an empty landing spot to jump. RULE: A valid jump requires an immediate neighbor to leap over, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Assuming grid coordinates match pixel positions directly; verify cell centers before clicking.

GOAL: Match the grid colors to the patterns shown in the two mini grids. CONTROLS: Click blocks to toggle their color between blue and orange. RULE: The top mini sets the top rows, the bottom mini sets the bottom rows, sharing the middle. TRAP: Assuming the middle row follows only one mini; it actually combines both, creating a conflict if ignored.

GOAL: Merge two pairs of pieces to form a new entity at the specific target location. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move pieces up to seven squares; click near two matching pieces to merge them. RULE: Merging happens instantly if your click is within range of both matching pieces, placing the result at your click. TRAP: Assuming you must physically move pieces together; you can merge from a distance if the click is close enough to both.

GOAL: Paint specific blocks orange based on hidden keys. CONTROLS: Click blocks to toggle their color. RULE: White pixels in a key dictate its center color; gray pixels force the other palette color. TRAP: Misaligning relative coordinates when mapping key pixels to blocks, leading to false conflicts.

GOAL: Shift colored blocks along fixed tracks to land yellow tokens on target brackets. CONTROLS: Click red nodes to rotate specific rows or columns in one direction. RULE: Each track is a closed loop, so items wrap around from one end to the other. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop at the edge; they cycle indefinitely, so over-rotation is possible.

ESTABLISHED: Blob speed is exactly half the token's dot count, rounded up. Parity rules apply. FAILED: Guessing hidden dot indices blindly causes the blob to miss the target by one step. GOAL IS NOT: Teleporting the token to the diamond center, as this displaces the required goal object. CONTROLS: Clicking a distant dot moves the token there and advances the blob by half that distance.

GOAL: Paint the grid cells to match the hidden color pattern. CONTROLS: Click keys to reveal their influence zones; click cells to cycle colors. RULE: White marks the key's own color; green marks the adjacent key's color. TRAP: Assuming green means "no change" or a specific third color wastes moves.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks exist in a uniform corridor maze. A HUD displays two white bars that grow as moves are made, potentially indicating progress or a countdown. FAILED: Moving blocks to specific symmetric coordinates (halves, corners, center) and attempting simple swaps did not clear the level. No trails were observed during movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply merging the blocks at the bottom center, as a wall blocks that area. It is also not a pathfinding task to specific empty "socket" cells. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move the blocks. The HUD bars reacted to these movements, changing pixel

ESTABLISHED: The exit corridor aligns with the block's current column, not the center. The path upward is clear if you stay left of the visual center. FAILED: Pressing UP from the center alignment fails; it hits a wall. Assuming the corridor was centered was a mistake. GOAL IS NOT: To reach the visual center of the maze top. The exit is offset to the left relative to the flag. CONTROLS: Up moves the block vertically. Right moves it horizontally. Stay in column 34 to fit the corridor.

GOAL: Push the green block up the narrow vertical corridor into the top box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block one step in the pressed direction. RULE: The block only moves if the entire path is clear of walls. TRAP: Assuming the block could squeeze through gaps narrower than its width.

GOAL: Place two matching shapes onto two identical blobs. CONTROLS: Click to drag the nearest shape within range. RULE: Shapes snap to blobs only when centered and fully inside. TRAP: Assuming any click in range moves the target; it may grab the wrong shape if too close to another.

GOAL: Place the yellow block at its bracket and the orange block at its matching bracket. CONTROLS: Left and right buttons rotate two separate rings of cells. RULE: Two cells are shared by both rings, so rotating either ring moves tokens located there. TRAP: Assuming shared cells belong to only one ring causes you to lose track of moving blocks.

ESTABLISHED: One square is controlled at a time; clicking a square swaps control. Uncontrolled squares slide until hitting walls or rings. FAILED: Moving only one square to a ring center does not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Placing a single square on a ring, nor matching specific dot colors. CONTROLS: Click a square to make it the active, movable piece. Arrow keys move the active square.

GOAL: Place both squares into the two rings at the same time. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active square; clicking swaps which square is active. RULE: Only the active square moves; the inactive square stays put until clicked. TRAP: Assuming you must keep one square fixed while solving the other; you must switch control to position both.

ESTABLISHED: Pressing SPACE creates a gray twin at the marked cell. The twin's behavior changes based on movement direction relative to the mark. FAILED: Assuming the twin always mirrors the blue block's path or moves with a fixed delay. Static twin positions in some trials contradicted movement-based theories. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the level by moving the blue block alone, nor is the twin a permanent obstacle. CONTROLS: SPACE toggles a marker mode. Moving away from the mark spawns or shifts the gray twin, while moving toward it may clear the marker.

GOAL: Capture the moving blob by landing your token exactly on its position. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the token to a distant spot, which simultaneously pushes the blob along its path. RULE: The blob moves half as fast as your token, so closing the distance requires strategic spacing rather than direct pursuit. TRAP: Believing you can chase the blob in small steps fails; short moves let the blob escape, requiring long, calculated jumps instead.

GOAL: Push each block to the opposite starting side. CONTROLS: Left arrows move the left block; right arrows move the right block. RULE: Blocks must cross the center divide to swap positions. TRAP: Trying to merge blocks in the middle fails; they must pass through to the other half.

GOAL: Place the mirrored piece onto the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the piece three cells per press. RULE: The target matches the mirror orientation, so the mirrored piece must land there, not the original. TRAP: Believing the black piece itself needed to reach the yellow spot wasted time testing rotations and direct paths.

GOAL: Align the player and mirror symmetrically across the divider to match the target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; Space switched selection between the player and the divider. RULE: The mirror’s position is always calculated as the reflection of the player across the divider’s current line. TRAP: Assuming the divider is static; you must select it and move it to shift the axis of symmetry.

GOAL: Move two blocks to occupy the same cell to trigger a win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: If both blocks attempt to enter the same empty tile, the level is cleared immediately. TRAP: Assuming blocks block each other prevents progress; they actually pass through or ignore collision unless the target is the same cell.

GOAL: Slide the plug right until both prongs touch the socket tabs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug piece across the grid. RULE: Completion requires simultaneous contact between both plug tips and their matching sockets. TRAP: Assuming one connected prong meant success; partial contact does not finish the level.

ESTABLISHED: The token occupies rows 30-31, cols 20-21. The red piece's remaining cells (rows 32-33, cols 12-17) are the only viable rotation source to fill the vertical gap above the token. FAILED: Moving directly upward is blocked by charcoal cells. Previous attempts to navigate around the gap without rotating the red piece failed. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the gap's left side or using the already-consumed gray trail cells for vertical movement. CONTROLS: Clicking the red plug rotates the remaining red cells. The transform maps the red remnant to rows 24-29, cols 20-21, creating a path upward.

GOAL: Capture three red sentinels by moving into their cells, then reach the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; entering a sentinel’s cell removes it. RULE: Sentinels attack only from their facing direction if you are adjacent there. TRAP: Assuming any adjacency triggers an attack wastes time; only the facing side is dangerous.
GOAL: Clear the path by swapping obstacles. CONTROLS: Click blue items to swap positions. RULE: Pieces restore full shape when moved. TRAP: Thinking eaten pieces stay damaged forever.

ESTABLISHED: The block has 55 purple and 45 white pixels. The cup currently holds purple ink. FAILED: Pouring from various angles failed to paint the entire block purple, leaving twenty cells white. GOAL IS NOT: Requiring the block to be completely purple, as full coverage is geometrically impossible. CONTROLS: Clicking ink slots changes the cup's color. Pouring paints triangular regions on the block.

GOAL: Align moving shapes with their reflected counterparts across a central divider line. CONTROLS: Arrows shift active pieces; Space switches which piece is controlled. RULE: Pieces reflect instantly across the divider, so positioning one dictates the other’s location. TRAP: Assuming pieces pass through targets; they stop at boundaries, wasting moves if not planned.

ESTABLISHED: The boat is currently docked at the leftmost outline. The blue section sits at columns 32-33, with yellow at column 34. FAILED: Pressing LEFT moved the boat to the left outline but did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the boat to the left edge is not the solution. CONTROLS: LEFT moves the boat one outline position to the left.

GOAL: Mirror two shapes across a movable divider line to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece or divider. Space cycles selection between them. RULE: Pieces reflect perfectly across the divider, so aligning one side automatically fills the other. TRAP: Assuming pieces cannot pass through each other during movement. Overlapping is allowed and often necessary.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the patrolling guard and the red hazard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step per turn. RULE: The guard walks a fixed eight-step loop up and down column three. TRAP: Assuming the guard’s pattern resets or is random wastes turns; it is a strict, predictable cycle.

GOAL: Slide pieces so every red tip overlaps another to turn gray. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece, Space rotates it, and Clicks select a new piece. RULE: Overlapping tips become gray, signaling a successful connection. TRAP: The selected piece turns white, hiding its true color and confusing identification.

GOAL: Paint the target block by moving a cup around obstacles to pour colors from specific angles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the cup’s position around the center; Space pours the selected color; Clicks switch colors. RULE: The cup pours only into the half-plane facing away from the center, so position dictates coverage area. TRAP: Assuming free rotation caused dead ends; movement is restricted to a fixed arc, requiring careful path planning to switch sides.

GOAL: Reach the target square while navigating a grid filled with four moving enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the character one step up, down, left, or right. RULE: You could only move into a square if no enemy occupied it now or would occupy it on the next turn. TRAP: Assuming enemies moved only once per turn caused failures; they shift positions instantly with every action, requiring precise timing.

GOAL: Guide the token through rotating barriers to reach the yellow exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token; the red button rotates specific wall segments. RULE: Walls only shift when the button is pressed, creating temporary bridges or gaps. TRAP: Assuming the path is static wastes time; you must rotate the red walls to align the bridge with the exit corridor.

GOAL: Paint the grid with three colors to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cup. Space poured ink. Clicks selected colors. RULE: Ink covers cells on the cup's side of the center line. TRAP: Pouring the final color first hides previous layers, ruining the pattern.

GOAL: Move the yellow token to the yellow bracket and the orange token to the orange bracket in the bottom-right corner. CONTROLS: Top and bottom arrows rotate the vertical ring of blocks; left and right arrows rotate the horizontal ring. RULE: The two rings intersect at four center cells, allowing you to transfer tokens between the vertical and horizontal paths. TRAP: Assuming the rings are independent prevents you from using the shared center cells to switch tokens from one track to the other.

GOAL: Clear the path so the boat floats up and reaches the pink target. CONTROLS: Click removes blocks; arrows move the boat horizontally. RULE: The boat always rises to the highest open water column after any action. TRAP: Thinking clicks only remove blocks without moving the boat; they actually trigger an immediate ascent.

GOAL: Align the piece and its three mirror reflections to completely fill the target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected divider or piece; Space cycles between the three objects. RULE: The four shapes only lock when they perfectly cover the area with no gaps or overlaps. TRAP: Ignoring that dividers must be positioned first to define the reflection axes before moving the piece.

GOAL: Rotate eight glyph tiles until each matches its assigned color group. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selection cursor; UP rotates the selected tile’s glyphs. RULE: Pressing UP rotates all glyphs within a tile simultaneously to align them. TRAP: Selection brackets change width for wider tiles, so assuming fixed cursor coordinates causes navigation errors.

GOAL: Guide the ink blob into the head's cavity. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the entire blob two squares per press. RULE: The blob rotates as it moves, so plan paths that fit the narrow channel. TRAP: Assuming the blob stays aligned; ignoring rotation causes jams in tight spots.

GOAL: Move two yellow tokens to their matching bracketed targets. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate the top row; bottom arrows rotate the long snake path. RULE: The top row is part of the snake, so moves interact on shared cells. TRAP: Treating the top row and snake as separate, independent puzzles.

GOAL: Clear the board by capturing all red guards and reaching the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your piece one step at a time. RULE: You can only capture a guard if you approach from a direction perpendicular to where they face. TRAP: Moving into a cell a guard currently faces causes instant failure, even if they are about to be captured.

GOAL: Align three blocks by clearing overlaps to reach targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; clicks select a block. RULE: Only the topmost visible part of a block can be clicked to select it. TRAP: Assuming you can click a block’s center if it is partially covered by another block.

GOAL: Paint a specific multi-colored geometric pattern on the central block by layering distinct ink pours. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cup to pour positions; clicks select ink colors or the final stamp; spacebar applies the current ink. RULE: Each pour position covers a unique half-plane, so the final color of any cell is determined solely by the last ink poured there. TRAP: Assuming pours blend or stack transparently; they do not, so order matters critically to avoid overwriting required colors.

GOAL: Place tokens on portals and swap their positions. CONTROLS: Click cross arms to rotate tokens; click center to swap. RULE: Each arm click rotates the ring of tokens by one step. TRAP: Assuming all arms rotate the same direction; they alternate clockwise and counter-clockwise.

GOAL: Fill four zones with specific colors and stamp a yellow block. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the cup; clicks selected ink or the stamp; space poured ink. RULE: Pour orange before purple, as their regions overlap in a way that breaks the pattern if reversed. TRAP: Trying to pour purple first seems efficient but forces extra moves later because no valid orange pour exists afterward.

GOAL: Join all four shapes into a single connected block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks select a new piece. RULE: Pieces only stick together when their pointed tips touch exactly. TRAP: Moving a piece without first clicking it does nothing, wasting turns.

GOAL: Place yellow tokens on the marked corner and center cells. CONTROLS: Up and down arrows rotate a vertical trio. Left and right arrows rotate a long horizontal line and a small square box simultaneously. RULE: The corner cell belongs to both the vertical trio and the horizontal line, allowing vertical moves to shift the horizontal sequence. TRAP: Treating the vertical and horizontal groups as separate, independent puzzles instead of recognizing their shared cell connection.

GOAL: Fill the block by pouring paint from four positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cup, clicks select paint, space pours. RULE: Each position pours a specific half-plane, like a triangle. TRAP: Assuming the diagonal pour is symmetric to the others without verifying.

GOAL: Guide the token from the start to the yellow box by creating a bridge through red and purple zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token one step; clicks toggle block states to open or close paths. RULE: Solid blocks allow passage, while empty gaps block movement, requiring specific toggles to connect isolated regions. TRAP: Assuming all toggles help; clicking red too early or incorrectly can seal the bridge, forcing a long backtrack.

GOAL: Move scattered squares into their matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected square; clicks select a square. RULE: Only the currently selected square moves; others stay still. TRAP: Clicking a square near the board's edge may appear to do nothing, but it actually selects it.

GOAL: Clear the level by merging matching blocks within three moves. CONTROLS: Click near a block to move or merge it; click elsewhere to push the hazard ring away. RULE: The shrinking ring consumes any block it touches, so maintain distance while pursuing merges. TRAP: Assuming a click only affects the targeted block, ignoring how nearby blocks also shift or merge simultaneously.

ESTABLISHED: The token pushes the blob away along the connecting corridor. The blob moves roughly 70 percent of the token's distance. FAILED: Attempting to force the blob into the ring by clicking adjacent to it caused no movement or wrong direction. GOAL IS NOT: Simply swapping the token and diamond positions, nor moving the token directly onto the ring. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot moves the token to that spot, pushing the blob if the path intersects it.

ESTABLISHED: Bar at col 2 moves left 1 cell; stem at col 1 moves up 1 cell; clamping occurs at walls. FAILED: Testing magnitudes at rightmost columns; assuming uniform vector sums; rotating about center without shift. GOAL IS NOT: A simple linear path or fixed-magnitude translation independent of column position. CONTROLS: Clicking switches toggles bars/stems; ball executes resulting vector sum with edge clamping and possible rotation shifts.

GOAL: Guide the sliding cross into the matching ring hole using arrow keys. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block to push the cross. RULE: A piece already overlapping a ring slides freely until it hits the hole. TRAP: Thinking the cross would stop at the first ring edge; it must fully enter to snap in.

GOAL: Place two shapes to cover matching colored dots, ensuring each shape covers only its own color. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space switches between the Plus and X shapes. RULE: A shape’s color changes only when it touches a matching color box, not merely by proximity. TRAP: Assuming shapes can share coverage; they cannot overlap dots of different colors, forcing separate paths.

ESTABLISHED: The boat travels horizontally and rises only when water exists above. FAILED: Moving the boat left through the lower gap without first clearing the overhead block row caused a stall or death. GOAL IS NOT: Simply navigating to the left side of the current water level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the boat; clicking removes adjacent blocks.

ESTABLISHED: The red bar’s top pushes the wall down, which squeezes the orange block, which then presses the solid block downward. FAILED: Short red bar lengths fail to push the solid block low enough for the side wall to reach the target columns. GOAL IS NOT: Just moving the wall horizontally; the wall must descend fully while the solid block is pushed down simultaneously. CONTROLS: Clicking red shrinks it (pushing things down), while clicking blue, orange, sky, and pink adjusts their sizes or positions.

GOAL: Guide two blocks to collide at the same cell to clear the level. CONTROLS: Up and down move both blocks together; left and right move them in opposite directions. RULE: One block moves normally while the other is mirrored horizontally, forcing coordinated movement to reach shared targets. TRAP: Assuming both blocks respond identically to left and right commands wastes moves when one actually reverses direction.

ESTABLISHED: Liquid rises if open above, spreading sideways only when blocked. With the current paddle, a stream cannot reach the middle slot from the sides. FAILED: Trying to fill all three containers simultaneously is impossible with only two streams. Sideways spreading stops at gaps. GOAL IS NOT: Filling every container. The win condition likely involves touching the red bars, not just filling pots. CONTROLS: Paddle position dictates where streams rise. Streams split at the paddle edges, turning up at open columns.

ESTABLISHED: The arm extends horizontally to push blocks; contact causes a visual flash. FAILED: Extending the arm while uncollected blocks are attached to the body does not trigger collection. GOAL IS NOT: Collecting a block simply by touching it with the arm tip. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the arm's base; extending the arm pushes blocks forward along the row.

GOAL: Slide the cross shape up into the ring’s hole at the top of the board. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks select which piece to control. RULE: Pushing a piece into another slides the target until it overlaps a boundary or snaps into a catch. TRAP: Assuming one push seats the piece; partial overlaps require repeated pushes to clear the obstruction and snap it home.

GOAL: Move two blocks into the same cell to merge them. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move all blocks simultaneously; the right block moves opposite to your input. RULE: Park the dot in a corner first, then push blocks toward the center corridor until they collide. TRAP: Forgetting the right block's inverted controls leads to wasted moves and failed collisions.

GOAL: Cycle through three shapes to recolor specific grid zones and reach the finish. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space cycles selection between X, Diamond, and Plus. RULE: A shape only recolors cells its pixels physically touch, allowing precise layering of colors. TRAP: Assuming shapes share movement paths wastes turns; each shape requires a unique route to cover its target area efficiently.

ESTABLISHED: The orange places F5 at (7,3) via column 2. F1 can be placed at (8,3) without blocking this path. F2 lands at (9,3) or (8,3) when dragged via row 10. FAILED: Dropping F1 at (8,3) with SPACE did not work as expected. Attempting to place F2 manually exceeded the step limit. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the entire container with orange. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. SPACE toggles frame attachment or drops it.

GOAL: Float the plug into the third compartment, then raise it to the ceiling. CONTROLS: Click gates to transfer the plug; press buttons to shift fluid between adjacent compartments.
